subject: Congress
note: Establishes regulatory framework for permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Requires 100% reserve backing with liquid assets.

subject: GENIUS Act
note: 100% reserve backing with U.S. dollars, short-term Treasuries, or equivalent liquid assets. Monthly public reserve disclosures.

subject: GENIUS Act
object: demand for U.S. debt and dollar reserve status
note: White House fact sheet states Act intended to cement dollar reserve-currency status.

subject: OCC
object: GENIUS Act implementation for national banks
note: Proposed rulemaking for payment stablecoin activities by national banks and federal savings associations.

subject: OCC
note: National banks may hold crypto-assets as principal and pay network fees as incidental to permissible banking activities.

subject: Treasury/FinCEN
note: Permitted payment stablecoin issuers treated as financial institutions under Bank Secrecy Act. AML, sanctions, KYC required.

subject: Federal Reserve
note: Fed notes stablecoins designed to maintain 1:1 value relative to USD. Analyzes cross-border payment implications.

subject: Richmond Fed
note: If stablecoins are credibly backed by safe dollar assets, adoption raises demand for Treasuries and dollar-denominated safe assets.

subject: SEC
note: Blockchain representation does not remove federal securities-law obligations. Transfer agent, custody, compliance requirements persist.

subject: FDIC
note: GENIUS Act makes clear payment stablecoins are NOT deposit-insured or guaranteed by U.S. government. Cannot claim FDIC backing.

subject: DTCC
note: Extending trusted market infrastructure into digital assets within regulated ecosystem.

subject: Bullish
note: $4.2B all-stock acquisition. ~3,000 public companies. Accelerates tokenized securities with 24/7 trading, stablecoin payments, instant settlement.

subject: Bank of England
note: Governor Bailey warns stablecoins could create financial-stability risks if not consistently regulated, especially around convertibility during stress.

subject: Federal Reserve Board
object: Federal Reserve not owned by anyone
note: Board of Governors is a federal agency accountable to Congress. Member bank stock cannot be sold, traded, or pledged. Not like corporate ownership.

subject: U.S. Treasury
note: Primary dealers are trading counterparties of NY Fed. Expected to bid in Treasury auctions at reasonably competitive prices.

subject: New York Fed
object: open-market operations in Treasury secondary market
note: Buys and sells Treasury securities for System Open Market Account under FOMC authorization. Implements monetary policy.

subject: foreign holders
note: Japan ~$1.239T, UK ~$897B, China ~$693B. Foreign holdings at record highs in Feb 2026 even as China trimmed.

subject: foreign Treasury holders
note: Foreign Treasury holdings hit record highs in February 2026 even as China reduced exposure.
